title: My Chinese Custom Build vs Specialized Tarmac SL8 - Superbike KILLER?

takeaways.text: He describes RDC as SEKA's lightweight version and repeats a claimed 685 g frame weight; his size L uses the regular fit, one of two fit options, the other having a much lower stack.
The one-piece Rapier bar routes the brake hoses and Di2 internally; his is 130 mm by 38 cm with slight flare, and the frame takes proprietary aero cages for round bottles.
He found it comfortable for an all-round race bike, with rear-end comfort closer to his Tarmac SL7 than to the SL8.
Downsides he found: the supplied bottle cages have a sharp edge, and the derailleur hanger can shift when the rear wheel is removed, so the thru-axle may not engage until the hanger is realigned.
He notes that a custom build needs someone to check compatibility and assemble it, that the labour belongs in the budget, and that lesser-known parts may not fit as intended.

disclosure: The video contains paid promotion for an insurer that sponsors the channel's tech show; the presenter calls this his own custom build, and how the frame and parts were obtained is not stated.
summary: A March 2026 Cycling Weekly custom build on a size L SEKA Spear RDC frameset with Shimano Dura-Ace, compared by feel with the presenter's Specialized Tarmac SL8. It covers one build and its parts choices.
